summary: Fixed QA-2: strengthened the R8 split-control programmatic-sweep test in __tests__/ZestButtonFocusSheen.test.tsx. It now asserts the parity class (sheenTriggerOdd/Even) lands on the split wrapper, that a later trigger change swaps parity so the sweep restarts, and that the split overlay rules .focusSheenSplit.sheenProgrammatic.sheenTriggerOdd/Even::before reference the alternating zestFocusSheenSweep / zestFocusSheenSweepAlt keyframes. No production code changed.

tests.name: R6: a split button with focusSheen suppresses the chevron mount streak and shows only the whole-control layer
R6: a split button given a sheenTrigger suppresses the chevron mount streak
R6: regular buttons have no mount streak and gain no extra chevron layer
R6: a split button mounted and then immediately focused shows only the whole-control layer
R6: a trigger change inside the old mount-streak window adds no second chevron streak
R6: a split button that does not use the sheen keeps its one-time chevron mount streak
R7: the value on mount plays nothing and the first change plays one sweep on an unfocused button
R7: changing while a sweep is playing restarts it (parity flips)
R7: works with focusSheen omitted, false and true
R7: a trigger while focused plays the programmatic layer as well as the focus layer
R7: repeated triggers after the animation has ended still replay
R8: a split control sweeps once across the whole control per trigger change
R8: a disabled button plays one sweep without becoming usable or firing its click handler
R8: a busy button plays a sweep and keeps its aria-busy and spinner state
R8: a disabled button never shows a focus streak
R8: a button that is both disabled and busy plays exactly one sweep per change
R8: the sweep is not restarted when the busy state ends part-way
R8: the band is visible on the disabled colours of every style
R8: the band is visible on the disabled colours of outline, text and dashed buttons
R9: reduced motion removes both bands entirely, with no override
R9: the rule is a live media query applied to regular, split and both triggers
R9: reduced motion leaves the focus ring and other feedback alone
A1: reduced motion disables the focus streak for regular and split buttons
A1: the value on the first render is inactive and plays nothing
A1: each later value change returns an alternating active result, including number to string
A2: an opted-in split control suppresses the chevron mount streak
A2: two identical keyframes exist and odd/even reference a different one
